newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt offers up to 90 percent of Kahromica.
newsitem.headline: Egypt offers up to 90 percent of Kahromica.

text.p: The Egyptian state on Sunday offered for sale by auction at least 200,000 shares in Egypt Company for Mechanical and Electrical Projects (KAHROMICA), 10 percent of the company's total equity.

The shares on sale to an anchor investor can be increased to a maximum of 1.8 million shares, representing up to 90 percent of equity, the state's Holding Company for Electric Power Distribution and Construction said in an announcement.
New shareholders will be eligible for the cash distribution for the financial year 1996/7, which ends on June 30. It did not say how much the coupon would be.
Priority will be given to bidders with relevant qualifications and previous experience, Misr International Bank (MIBank) senior general manager Mohammed Ozalp told Reuters.
Winning the auction also depends on the number of shares sought and the price offered, Ozalp added.
Sealed bids should be addressed to the head of the financial, administrative and economic affairs sectors at the holding company in Medinet Nasr, northeast of Cairo.
The deadline for bids is noon (1000 GMT) on Thursday, May 15, said the holding company, which owns KAHROMICA.
MIBank and the brokerage firm International Investors will act as agents for the auction.
More details are available from MIBank.
